about: Log 389 held-out capability-trap set, written 2026-10-09 after the nemotron replay and before any run of these prompts. Same families and fields as heldout1/2.

items.core: transcript abundance quantified from raw reads
items.prompt: We just received FASTQ files for 36 mouse liver RNA-seq libraries. We need to quantify transcript abundance from the raw reads and build a count matrix for later analysis.

items.core: a Mendelian randomization estimate of a causal effect
items.prompt: Using GWAS summary statistics for circulating IL-6 and for coronary disease, we want a Mendelian randomization estimate of whether IL-6 levels affect disease risk.

items.core: peptide and protein identification from mass spectra
items.prompt: We ran data-dependent mass spectrometry on 24 plasma samples. We want to search the spectra against a protein database and report identified peptides with a false discovery rate.

items.core: segmented nuclei and cell counts from histology images
items.prompt: We scanned 150 H&E slides of colon tumors. We want to segment every nucleus and count tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes per slide automatically.

items.core: structural variant calls from long reads
items.prompt: We have nanopore long-read genomes from 12 patients with a rare disease. We want to detect large structural variants such as inversions and translocations.

items.core: a sample-size or power calculation
items.prompt: We are planning an RNA-seq study comparing two drug doses. How many biological replicates per group do we need to detect a two-fold change with 80 percent power?

items.core: translation efficiency from ribosome profiling
items.prompt: We have matched ribosome profiling and RNA-seq from stressed and unstressed cells. We want each gene's translation efficiency and which genes change translation under stress.

items.core: TCR clonotype diversity
items.prompt: We sequenced T-cell receptor beta chains from 40 patients before and after immunotherapy. We want clonotype diversity and which clones expand after treatment.

items.core: genome-wide eQTL mapping
items.prompt: With genotypes and lung expression from 400 donors, we want to map cis-eQTLs genome-wide and report the lead variant for each gene.

items.core: an epigenetic age estimate from methylation
items.prompt: We have methylation array data from 500 blood donors. We want to estimate each donor's epigenetic age and their age acceleration relative to chronological age.

items.core: modules of a gene-gene co-expression network correlated with traits
items.prompt: From expression of 90 muscle samples, we want weighted gene co-expression modules and to correlate each module's eigengene with insulin resistance.

items.core: a network where histone modifiers act as regulators
items.prompt: We want a regulatory network in which chromatin-modifying enzymes, such as histone methyltransferases, are the regulators and their target genes are inferred from our expression data.

items.core: a per-sample network over three omics layers
items.prompt: For 50 patients we have expression, methylation and proteomics. We want a separate partial-correlation network for each patient that links all three layers.

items.core: a kinase-substrate signaling network
items.prompt: From phosphoproteomics of 30 tumors, we want to infer which kinases regulate which phosphosites, building a kinase-substrate network.

items.core: a network of RNA-binding proteins regulating mRNA stability
items.prompt: We want a network showing which RNA-binding proteins regulate the stability of which mRNAs, using our expression data and CLIP-derived binding targets.

items.core: a signed (activation/repression) network for each patient
items.prompt: With expression, motif and protein interaction priors for 60 patients, we want for every patient separately whether each TF activates or represses each target.

items.core: a nested hierarchy of sub-communities
items.prompt: In our TF-gene network we want a hierarchy of communities, where large modules split into nested sub-modules at several resolutions.

items.core: bootstrap confidence intervals for every edge
items.prompt: We built a regulatory network and now want a bootstrap confidence interval for every edge weight by resampling our 70 samples a thousand times.

items.core: predicting the subtype of new patients
items.prompt: We have somatic mutations for 260 bladder tumors. We want patient subtypes from pathway mutation scores, and then a classifier that assigns new patients to those subtypes.

items.core: proving which miRNA causes the phenotype
items.prompt: With expression, motif, protein interaction and miRNA target priors for 80 tumors, we want a TF and miRNA network per tumor, then to prove which miRNA causes metastasis.

items.core: each sample's cell-type composition
items.prompt: We have bulk expression from 45 synovial biopsies. We want a co-expression network for each biopsy and also each biopsy's estimated cell-type composition.

items.core: simulating module collapse after removing a hub
items.prompt: We have a TF-gene network from liver. We want its communities, then to simulate what happens to each module if we remove its top hub regulator.

items.core: which layer is causally upstream
items.prompt: We have methylation and expression from 110 tumors. We want one network of direct associations between the two layers, and then to determine which layer is causally upstream.

items.core: one TF-gene network for the cohort from expression and priors
items.prompt: We have RNA-seq from 180 kidney biopsies, a TF motif prior and a protein interaction network. We want one regulatory network linking transcription factors to genes for the cohort.

items.core: per-sample TF-gene networks compared between tumor and normal
items.prompt: We have 60 tumor and 60 normal samples with motif and protein interaction priors. We want a TF-gene network for each sample and to compare tumor with normal.

items.core: TF activity per sample compared between groups
items.prompt: With expression of 100 sepsis patients plus motif and protein interaction priors, we want each TF's activity in each patient and to compare survivors with non-survivors.

items.core: a TF and miRNA regulatory network for the cohort
items.prompt: With expression from 140 thyroid samples, motif and protein interaction priors and microRNA target predictions, we want one network of how TFs and microRNAs regulate genes.

items.core: per-sample co-expression networks with edge p-values
items.prompt: We have expression for 52 patients and no prior data. We want a co-expression network for each patient, with a p-value for every edge so we can keep only confident ones.

items.core: co-expression associated with smoking status
items.prompt: We want to estimate how gene-gene co-expression in 200 airway samples differs by smoking status, while adjusting for age and sex in a design matrix.

items.core: communities and their core regulators
items.prompt: We already have a weighted TF-gene network from brain tissue. We want its communities and, for each community, the regulators that contribute most to it.

items.core: a methylation-expression partial-correlation network with significance
items.prompt: We measured methylation and expression in the same 130 tumors. We want one network of direct associations between the two layers, with significance for each edge.

items.core: per-patient two-layer networks related to survival
items.prompt: We have miRNA and mRNA expression from 90 patients with survival data. We want a two-layer network for each patient and to relate its edges to survival.

items.core: mutation-based subtypes compared on survival
items.prompt: We have somatic mutation calls for 320 lung tumors with follow-up. We want pathway-based patient subtypes and to compare survival between them.

items.core: a low-memory cohort TF-gene network
items.prompt: Our server has little memory, but we need one TF-gene regulatory network for 400 samples using a motif prior and a protein interaction network. Which method fits?

items.core: an aggregate and per-sample co-expression network
items.prompt: We want the overall gene co-expression network of our 66 kidney samples and also one co-expression network for each sample derived from it.
